mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in PARKS mobility acts as a leading indicator of broader discretionary out-of-home activity, so a sustained increase in PARKS over the next month will lift RETAIL_REC relative to the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS turned positive at t-0w after being negative in the prior three weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS does not remain above its last-4-week average while RETAIL_REC still falls over the next 28 days, this leading-signal hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated, more time at home substitutes away from shopping trips and discretionary errands, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next 1-2 weeks as residential activity rises.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains at least 1 point above its t-3w level for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is positive in all four observed weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week average within two weeks, the substitution mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT increases access to shopping areas and raises pass-through exposure to retail districts, so a week-on-week rise in TRANSIT should translate into a higher RETAIL_REC level over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week from a prior trough
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -34.1 at t-1w to -30.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises from a trough but RETAIL_REC does not improve versus the prior four weeks over the next month, the access mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain deeply negative, commuting-linked shopping stays suppressed and retail visitation will remain below the prior four-week mean over the next month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both stay below -30 for at least two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series remain around -30 to -38 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay below -30 yet RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the commuting-suppression hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp PARKS rebound after a previously weak outdoor pattern signals improved weather or seasonality, and that seasonal uplift spills into discretionary shopping visits with a one-week lag.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from negative to positive week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -18.7 at t-1w to 5.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS turns positive but RETAIL_REC does not improve within one week, the seasonal spillover claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL indicates more local, necessity-oriented routines, which crowds out discretionary retail trips and pulls RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both increase for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL are both above baseline in the snapshot
failure_condition: If both proxies rise for two weeks but RETAIL_REC also rises above its last-4-week average, the local-routine substitution hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Under reopening conditions, improving mobility at WORKPLACES and TRANSIT loosens trip chaining and restores lunch and after-work shopping, so RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks when both series trend upward together.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -38.1 to -32.4 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve together but RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean over the next month, the trip-chaining mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week surge in PARKS followed by continued weakness in WORKPLACES identifies leisure substitution rather than broad recovery, so retail mobility should soften within the next four weeks once park activity dominates work travel.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above zero while WORKPLACES stays below -30
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS is positive at t-0w while WORKPLACES remains deeply negative
failure_condition: If PARKS stays positive and WORKPLACES stays below -30 but RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days, the leisure-substitution mechanism is rejected.
